searchText: One usecase I can imagine is a lightclient wanting to have faster access to a recent syncaggregate than with the current routes available, which have a delay of 4/3 slots. With that route, connecting to a beacon node subscribe to all sync subnets you can get a good sync aggregate 1/3 into the slot Hi! Looking at the `eventstream` `examples` from the beacon-APIs spec, I can see some payload being wrapped in a `data` element with an associated `version` (e.g. `light_client_optimistic_update`, `payload_attributes`) while others are not. see https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/eventstream/index.yaml#L47 Is there some logic allowing to distinguish both form? as in a validator in the index range, or a validator beyond the index range? so if we're at max 1 mil and i try to select 2 mil? probably to allow the version field to travel along side, but this is just an educated guess Possibly would be nice to understand why those 2 specific events needed version attached, theres probably discussions in the initial PRS that added them ref. https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/305 but no reasoning that I found...
